there was never new economics along with the new economy sure there was lot talk about increasing returns network effects switching costs and but these are hardly new concepts they been part the economics literature for decades furthermore although these are important ideas they aren big ideas they explain certain phenomena well but they have limited reach those search really big idea had look further back the economics literature they hit gold with the nature the firm paper written the nobel laureate ronald coase coase paper asked deceptively simple question the market such great tool for allocating resources why isn used inside the firm company why doesn one worker the assembly line negotiate with the worker next him about the price which will supply the partially assembled product that sort negotiation rarely happens instead using markets companies tend organized hierarchies using chain command and control rather than negotiation markets and explicit contracts paradoxically the primary unit capitalism close inspection looks lot like central planning coase didn just ask this question also provided provocative answer all hinges the costs making transactions what economists call firms said are essentially groups activities for which more effective and less costly use command and control than markets have things done new economy advocates found this compelling idea one consequence the internet has surely been make cheaper communicate this should turn lower transaction costs and change company boundaries their conclusion was that companies would inevitably downsize and outsource spinning off unnecessary functions and carry out more and more transactions using the internet instead internal memos not fast the internet lowers communication costs that for sure but that means lowers transaction costs within organizations well across organizations the internal memo might disappear but only because replaced the internal mail just doesn follow that lower communication costs lead smaller companies fact coase himself said that changes like the telephone and telegraphy which tend reduce the cost organizing spatially will tend increase the size the firm there lot other evidence the economics literature for coase observation the harvard business historian alfred chandler classic work the visible hand documented how the deployment the telegraph and railroad led the creation the giant corporation maybe the internet role provide the inexpensive communications that can support megacorporations this thought enough make new economy guru shudder what the facts say about company size alas they are inconclusive from the average size company hardly budged and the small reduction that did occur could attributed the increased importance the service sector which tends have smaller companies later his article coase acknowledges that inventions like the telephone might reduce company size they reduce the costs using markets more than after the taliban fled western afghanistan word began spread about the new rulers herat the tajik tribesmen here allegedly were carrying out beatings arrests and robberies against ethnic pashtuns living and traveling the province the tales caused blood boil among their pashtun kinsmen some miles away kandahar country without strong central government working court system but gun almost every home sitting and stewing over problem not common practice for many pashtuns the stories injustice meant one thing fight just last week many afghans worried that post taliban civil war was brewing between the pashtuns kandahar and the tajiks herat but herat wednesday over lunch rice stewed lamb meatballs and tea afghanistan age old practice righting wrongs won out ismail khan herat warlord turned governor sat down with pashtun delegation elders discuss how calm the ethnic tensions that threatened peace the ongoing talks are promising sign that after more than two decades war the art politics may making comeback the preferred problem solving method afghanistan came town looking for peaceful solution came brothers not cause trouble and beat our chests but find result that good for all said haji abdul raof member the delegation from kandahar and helmand provinces the troubles began mid november when the taliban fled herat major trading city near the western border with iran the country only major highway connects herat kandahar and farther onward kabul the capital the ensuing power vacuum city residents most who are ethnic tajiks ganged ethnic pashtun businessmen looting some and arresting others witnesses said pashtun merchants the late 1990s had become some the richest storeowners town residents say because their ethnic ties with the taliban who also were pashtuns when khan was named governor herat province many expected stability western afghanistan but the streets did not get any safer for some pashtun residents said reports that iran was meddling local affairs and supporting khan troops also spread khan has denied any dealings with iran regardless stories circulated almost daily goods being confiscated and pashtun travelers being beaten and killed along the herat kandahar highway suddenly for the pashtuns safety was concern never before discussed whether travel along the road kandahar together whether was safe enough alone said mahai din achikzai used car dealer from kandahar who said lost five cars corrupt customs officials mid january least pashtuns had been arrested and others had cars homes other property stolen according the delegation herat this week three pashtuns reportedly had been killed afghans far away kabul viewed the situation the most serious threat afghanistan interim government especially when senior aide the pashtun governor kandahar gul agha sherzai told afghan radio that the governor was considering sending forces protect fellow pashtuns herat some fighters were reportedly amassed and ready march but pashtuns from kandahar and helmand provinces decided speak with khan before things deteriorated further country with telephones the parleying has done face face and delegates from kandahar and from helmand came deliver the message they set off sunday with armed person security detail herat miles the northwest motley diplomatic convoy toyota 4x4 trucks subaru station wagons and minivans was mission grave importance the blood was running high our land said raof aide sherzai needed settle the question whether innocent people had been arrested about who stole people property and how make the road safe for business the emissaries sent word khan monday morning that meeting was desired but typical afghan style reply was slow coming for hours the elders sat drinking endless cups tea and clicking prayer beads herat only hotel while the younger members the party grumbled that their patience was running out when word came that khan had invited them for lunch wednesday the group straightened their turbans slicked their beards and set off with piles hand written petitions and complaints the city military base both groups left their guns the door the building where they met participants said the group prayed together and khan gave warm welcome saying how important was treat each other brothers and then the verbal sparring began the pashtuns demanded better treatment their kinsman more guarantees for security the road and the release all pashtuns from jail khan countered that the problems were too large handle one afternoon and recommended inter regional committee earnings momentum strategies have been losing steam though too early count them out the strategies favor the stocks companies whose earnings are growing most rapidly while shunning even selling short those whose earnings are contracting the fastest all exploit the tendency investors respond slowly new information rather than reacting immediately strong earnings report for example investors often bid stock gradually those who use earnings momentum strategies can make profit reacting more quickly the profits have been large enough and enduring enough impress skeptical academics recently however the strategies have struggled according research ford investors services san diego stocks with the highest earnings momentum had one their worst years not only relative the market but also relative strategies based other popular stock selection tools like the price earnings ratio dividend yield relative strength the last three years stocks with the highest earnings momentum lagged the market more than they have over any other three year period since the editors the investment newsletters that monitor differ over what accounts for the recent struggles these strategies one hypothesis focuses the securities and exchange commission regulation which took effect regulation requires companies release material information publicly rather than privately wall street analysts some newsletter editors think that regulation reduces the market reaction time earnings information and therefore the profitability earnings momentum strategies many finance professors are skeptical about this hypothesis academic research suggests that deep rooted psychological factors cause investors react slowly new earnings information these factors have nothing with how companies communicate for example investors develop attachments stocks they love and revulsion those that have lost them money they assimilate contrary information slowly whether that information comes from analyst directly from the company another hypothesis earnings momentum strategies simply not work economic downturns the rationale that boom periods positive earnings momentum genuinely signals growth prospects downturns companies that buck the trend tend the best defensive players trait that admirable recession but that may have nothing with how well company performs over the long term also skeptical this hypothesis because there evidence suggesting that investors reaction times becomes speedier downturn fact the data suggest otherwise over the last years according ford investor services there were four other years besides which earnings momentum strategies lagged the average stock and the economy grew all four those years there another explanation for why earnings momentum strategies have languished may that many advisers and investors have started use earnings momentum strategies that they have begun kill the goose that lays the golden egg this the likely fate any strategy that becomes too popular and consistent with data showing that these strategies have found tougher recent years but premature conclude that this the case for earnings momentum given the strategies stellar long term record will take many more years mediocre performance convince statisticians that this recent experience not exception since the alternative giving the boot every strategy soon stops working approach that know does not work over time the intelligent bet the meantime for followers earnings momentum strategies should stick their guns

competitive strategy about being different means deliberately choosing different set activities deliver unique mix value writes michael porter bishop william lawrence university professor harvard university what strategy harvard business review november december business model the vehicle for operationalizing these differences harvard business school professors henry chesbrough and richard rosenbloom write recent working paper the business model describes the architecture the revenues but does far more than explain where the money will come from the discipline defining the business model creates framework for learning identifies the levers your disposal for carrying out strategy and encapsulates the norms beliefs and assumptions that help you make trade offs along the way well constructed business model focuses employees the activities that really add value accomplish that goal the business model must four things identify the customers you want serve specify the unmet latent needs the target market recession for instance individuals and institutions alike will need consulting legal and financial services related bankruptcy acquisitions and downsizing spell out how your business different from all the others its unique value proposition what product service you plan provide and why would anyone willing pay for demonstrate how your unique value proposition will address the market need you identified this you need consider customers employees and suppliers alike for customers the proposition may involve solving problem improving performance reducing risks and costs for employees and suppliers may include specialized training exclusive access research and development facilities continually growing workers knowledge and skills other ways building equity the business explain how you will implement the value proposition where will you get the raw materials required make your product will you build your own plant outsource the manufacturing alternatively what distribution networks will you rely generate requests for the service you intend provide how will you ensure that the people providing the actual service have the proper training creating and distributing accordance with your value proposition typically includes collaborating with other firms sometimes the collaboration horizontal when several the major automakers created joint initiative that enabled them purchase supplies more cheaply take hewlett packard integration its supply chain for computer monitors managing the entire process and sharing information with all the intermediate suppliers has been able cut costs and create higher levels product availability throughout the chain the business model should weigh the myriad alternatives the costs and trade offs involved with such collaboration strategies and describe the optimal configuration value chains and networks you need achieve what porter calls operational effectiveness addition the business model should identify which activities you want perform now and which you plan outsource discontinue altogether describe the profit patterns the associated cash flows and the attendant risks how and how much you expect customers pay when will the product service become profitable what will you ensure the sustainability those profits how will you divide the income among the business model participants revenues typically come from four broad categories selling your own products such pcs ordered and shipped directly from the maker small businesses and households stocking and selling the products other companies grocery stores and booksellers owning the infrastructure for example businesses that own the telecommunications platforms and utilities pipelines and providing access information services and the community like american express which gives third parties access all its cardholders either through advertising monthly billing statements referring cardholders the third party exchange for fee new business models must anticipate not only revenues and expenses they must also examine the timing magnitude and riskiness cash flows and the assumptions behind cardholders that financiers suppliers and customers alike can better gauge your ability deliver what you promised them updating your model there are some obvious times when you must reevaluate your model make sure there isn better way doing business when new product doesn fit your old paradigm classic examples include ibm feeble approach the market and firestone the radial tire market ibm existing model designed for selling mainframes didn allow imagine market for pcs firestone model geared for making bias tires couldn adjusted manufacture radials always thinking and talking about how you retool incorporate product innovation when existing product has entered new stage its product life cycle the business model needed launch innovative product differs dramatically from the one needed meet high demand once the product catches argues geoffrey moore his book inside the tornado consider the first harry potter book once word mouth got out the focus shifted from advertising and publicity inventory management distribution and licensing when the next big thing children literature comes along the publisher will flip the magician into maintenance mode plan new models around product passage through its life cycle when new technology threatens disrupt your model platform incumbents like charles schwab leader and long time innovator its field was slow embrace the internet partly because the commerce business model required entrepreneurial mindset but rather than develop the capabilities slowly within the existing model schwab launched entirely separate division that could free the established corporate culture once eschwab was and running however customers asked for seamless set services they didn want deal with two schwabs the company responded reintegrating the spin off when filling key position within the firm executing new different business model entrepreneurial act requiring high degree risk and requiring insight into both the technology and the market chesbrough and rosenbloom write managers can grease the wheels hiring people from diverse models not just for their technical marketing expertise but also for their experience managing through changing scenarios when the economy shifts during boom companies indiscriminately acquire customers talent suppliers and channels that may not add value the high maintenance low margin consumer who wastes your time but never buys anything immediately comes mind and today businesses are full them keep this check carefully review the models play and under construction put resources behind the most profitable ones and cut all the rest major historical era ending japan institutions that created the country economic miracle generation ago have now brought japan the verge economic debacle and the changes needed resolve that crisis will broadly affect the nation economy finances politics foreign policy and family life the roots the current malaise extend back the years between and when most the economic structures that still dominate japan today were created this system was developed rational way put japan economy wartime footing and served that purpose well also proved useful after the war the system functioned brilliantly for many years after japan surrender helping the country rebuild and leading years spectacular growth the same features that once did much good for japan however have now brought the nation the brink collapse thus the question today longer whether the country will reform its economy and finally abandon its wartime footing tokyo longer has any choice the question rather how japan will manage such radical change for the system has grown deeply entrenched all aspects japanese society wartime mobilization created many the practices now regarded distinctively japanese and wove them into the system among the changes introduced the japanese government were lifetime employment seniority pay company unions firms that gave priority employees over shareholders government policies that put banks before capital markets and the institutionalization policy coordination between government and corporations the general principles behind these arrangements fact were not very different from the ideas behind the centralization the economy during the war the difference that the japanese measures went much further and lasted lot longer until today fact course the system has undergone important changes the years since its creation for example the old family led zaibatsu which were dominated manufacturing companies have been replaced bank dominated groups known keiretsu management and labor unions have reached compact workers return for limited profit sharing have agreed not disrupt production japan economy has gradually become more market oriented but the core the system has endured for many years this extension the system into peacetime proved beneficial industries such steel production were already efficiently organized and had the technologies they needed what they similar periods last year one knows how many are sneaking undetected but officials expect the influx surge before the zimbabwean election set for march and fearful that civil unrest military coup might follow the voting the south african government preparing military base here house many refugees military officials say the exodus one reflection zimbabwe deepening political and economic woes once one the most prosperous countries africa zimbabwe now racked with food shortages surging unemployment and increasingly authoritarian government that seems more and more willing crack down its critics zimbabwe generals recently suggested that they would not support the opposition party candidate leading some officials here worry about possible coup others fear that opposition supporters most adults the state which suffered catastrophically after the collapse agriculture based economy the late 1920s and early 1930s oklahomans tended feel almost personal embarrassment about the underfed and undereducated heroes steinbeck novel social upheaval and migration the joad family who make the central characters the book migrate from eastern oklahoma california when they lose their farm they crude uneducated and times just not very smart part the problem with the grapes wrath for oklahomans the postwar generation may have been that steinbeck got much right thousands oklahomans faced with extreme deprivation headed west the late 1930s references cousins and old neighbors california were scattered through own childhood the 1960s followed teen age reading the grapes wrath about with questions for relatives about their sense the accuracy the book discovered that steinbeck had done pretty good job capturing the cantankerous rural poor the state only few decades earlier mother admitted that the compulsive sometimes self destructive behavior steinbeck joads and their neighbors reflected the actions many the rural poor she knew that era but the most painful part may have been that word okie though already existed steinbeck helped make the word okie permanent part the english language originally pejorative california for economic refugees from the southwest okie migrated back oklahoma nickname for residents the state the first okies out california doubtless forgot the label they moved into second generation and the old home state became nothing more than occasional christmas card from nearly forgotten relatives but for those who stayed behind oklahoma the label okie remained painful accusation joad like ignorance gradually oklahomans experiencing postwar prosperity and plenty thanks modern farming methods increased farm sizes federal subsidies and thriving petroleum industry began feel some distance from the joads only then were they able wear the okie label with good humor and look steinbeck book with interest and respect careful critical reading the grapes wrath these days reveals author with gift for poetic prose and knack for creating warm characters who although backward emerge with almost mythic bravery the face adversity little study the history the age however also reveals that the steinbeck the grapes wrath wasn much reporter historian makes huge errors sociology such asserting that tenant farmers like the joads might have been their land for decades when truth oklahoma had been settled recently and movement the tenant farmers that made most the state rural population was constant that any real life joads probably moved from one farm another every three years steinbeck also propagated that myth that the dust bowl drought instigated the great migration farm folk california there were numerous factors the migration but check the weather records eastern oklahoma the late 1930s the peak years migration proves that drought which had indeed been severe several hundred miles west the middle 1930s wasn one them nowadays oklahomans can read the grapes wrath without being embarrassed their depression era forbears those who moved california desperate and blindly faithful their own ability survive were indeed heroes the level steinbeck painted them those who stayed behind and built prosperous economy the ruins past era were equally brave and the children and grandchildren both can take pride the courage both and enjoy the grapes wrath for what novel human redemption that just happens set partly oklahoma relatives and friends life was very comfortable for then recalled recently would play polo the morning hunting for partridges the afternoon and the evening the dining room was always full never with less than people today lamas now the owner the estate the estancia delsel rather the little that remains less than tenth the original acreage still his hands and the cost maintaining the stately square foot manor house with its six bedrooms six bathrooms pool wine cellar and coach house not the same scale income said instead horses the estate here about miles northwest buenos aires now has only all but which belong boarders who pay lamas monthly fee where cattle once grazed some the most fertile pastureland the world lamas now hopes build small cottages where horse lovers can stay weekends and ride hike for more than century the estancia rural estate has been one the most elegant symbols argentina well one its principal sources wealth but the landed gentry who own those properties have long been decline and the country current economic crisis the worst its turbulent history only accelerating that process grandfather used say that even though the countryside squeezes doesn strangle lamas said but the breaking point the rural producing class debt its neck and struggling survive nearly years ago argentina made the peso and the dollar virtually interchangeable that research revealed the outlines how hair grows hair follicle forms the embryo are born with all the follicles ever have when the epidermis folds down into the underlying connective tissue dermis the narrow pocket that results filled with three concentric cylinders epidermal cells two root sheaths surround the hair shaft itself its base which growing adult hair about sixth inch below the skin protofibrils form cable called microfibril the microfibrils are bundled together into macrofibrils and bundle macrofibrils fills each hair cell the time the cell has moved one fiftieth inch upward from the dermal papilla choked with keratin fibers that longer exchanging material with its environment that dead well before even hits air individual hair typically grows for about three years bit less than half inch month the maximum length hair can reach around foot and half obviously there are lots atypical people when the growth phase ends the follicle rapidly shrivels and shrinks toward the surface the skin within three weeks the hair root only one fiftieth inch deep now enters rest phase about three months which comb even stiff breeze will rip out then miraculously the whole cycle begins again the follicle grows back down into the skin renews contact with the dermal papilla and starts producing new hair even more miraculous the follicles your head are all cycling through these phases completely independent one another and that good thing the follicles were synchronized our hairs would all fall out the same time and would molt instead each individual follicle seems have its own internal clock that drives from growth regression and back again still have clear idea whatsoever what this molecular clock paus says but fundamentally important find out because want change hair
